A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PFL-DocVQA competition. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, figures and equations support reliable comparison despite extensive relocation and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original baseline and participant experiments, including communication costs and ANLS scores in Tables 2–3, plus hyperparameter, quantization and optimizer studies in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Tables 2–7 and its appendices, and adds descriptive analysis of document counts per provider.

M1.justification: VT5, the organizer baselines, LoRA and quantization procedures, FedShampoo, and DP-CLGECL retain their components and update rules. The momentum variant already appeared in v1. Moving detailed descriptions into the main text does not introduce new methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PFL-DocVQA BLUE subset, invoice-question-answering tasks, ten clients, and seen/unseen-provider evaluation coverage. Pretraining data are unchanged. The new dataset-distribution figure introduces no additional training or evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the competition tables and supplementary studies, including tuned baselines and momentum variants. Newly discussed methods such as DP-Forward and DP-FTRL appear as related work, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Data splits, accuracy/ANLS metrics, communication accounting, privacy budgets and training configurations remain unchanged. Baseline and participant settings moved from v1's appendices into v2's main text. Expanded submission-review descriptions disclose procedures without establishing a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: New Figure A.2 characterizes imbalance in documents per provider within each client, supplementing the existing aggregate dataset statistics. The local-training, client-sampling, quantization, FedShampoo tuning and DP optimizer analyses are retained; their relocation does not constitute new ablations.

E5.justification: Seed and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged. The shared-RNG initialization statement remains in v1 Table A5/v2 Table 6, and the retained tuning and convergence plots are identical. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Figure A.2 adds provider-size distributions and identifies outliers with 531 documents in client 6 and 2283 in client 4. Matched model scores, rankings and communication costs are unchanged, including v1 Table 3/v2 Table 7 and v1 Tables A2–A5/v2 Tables 3–6.

T1.justification: The privacy definitions, RDP analysis, optimization equations and proofs retain their mathematical content. v1 Theorem B.9 becomes v2 Theorem 5.1, and appendix equations move into the main text. The expanded introductory DP explanation adds no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contribution: a private federated DocVQA competition/testbed and analysis of its solutions. The conclusion continues to present the benchmark and recommendations for future challenges. No central method or performance claim is replaced.

C2.justification: New takeaways discuss local epochs and client drift, parameter reduction, and the remaining private/non-private utility gap. Section 5.1 recharacterizes unchanged privacy budgets from medium/weak to strong/reasonable. The conclusion newly acknowledges absent empirical privacy attacks/audits, providers spanning multiple nodes being excluded, and simplified communication assumptions.

D1.justification: v2 adds the Track 2 winner's repository, changes Track 1 code from promised sharing to reported availability, and documents submission proof/code reviews and static checks. Conversely, Appendix A removes the direct dataset-download link and details about question templates, language-model rephrasing and manual annotation verification. Existing hardware and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused coverage of DP training methods and secure aggregation. New references also contextualize client drift, DocVQA leakage and DP implementation failures, including Karimireddy, Pinto and Ganev. The OpenAI reference disappears with the annotation-generation description; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: much of v1 Appendices C–D becomes Sections 4.3.1–4.3.3, 4.4.1 and 5.4.1, while baseline details and the main privacy theorem also move into the body. v2 adds takeaway subsections, expands background explanations, and rewrites and relocates author contributions.

P2.justification: v2 substantially changes typography and page layout, relocates four appendix tables into the main text, enlarges existing graphics, and separates algorithms and plots onto dedicated appendix pages. It adds boxed takeaways and the ten-panel provider-distribution figure. Retained plot content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the report easier to assess through integrated method details, explicit takeaways, clearer privacy-validation disclosures and concrete applicability limitations. Code-access statements and provider-distribution analysis add useful information. These gains are partly offset by removing annotation-generation and verification details. With the central experiments and theory unchanged, the net improvement is limited.
